incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Decree No. 67-236 of 23 March 1967 on commercial registry formalities; Code monétaire et financier Articles L.547-1 to L.547-12 and Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 for the regulated crowdfunding loan intermediation activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI single digital portal) and the territorial Registry of the Commercial Court (Greffe du Tribunal de commerce) of the department where the registered office is situated.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) executed in private deed or before a notary, submitted electronically via the 'Guichet unique' with the standardised incorporation application (formulaire M0), the bank or notarial certificate of cash capital deposit, the declaration of beneficial owner (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) and the attestation of publication of the legal announcement.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SAS; the share capital is freely fixed by the shareholders in the statuts. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and paid up prior to registration and must be escrowed with a French bank or a notary (dépôt des fonds) until the certificate of registration (Kbis) is issued. For the regulated P2P micro-lending permit, the ACPR additionally applies the own-funds requirement under Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 (EUR 25,000 or one quarter of fixed overheads, whichever is higher).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolution of the Sole Shareholder of [SAS], dated [date]: The shareholder unanimously resolves to (i) approve the subscription and paid-up capital allocation as specified in the Articles of Association; (ii) adopt the Articles of Association, with the registered office at [address]; (iii) appoint [Name] as Président with full statutory authority to represent the company; (iv) appoint [Name] as General Manager; (v) ratify the opening of bank accounts at [bank]; (vi) authorize the Président to file the incorporation with the Guichet Unique/INPI and the Commercial Court Registry; (vii) instruct the Président to apply for the ACPR crowdfunding authorization; and (viii) commence micro-lending operations only after all regulatory licenses are obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Association and Blocked Cash Capital Deposit (Constitution d'une SAS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders (private deed) and a commercial bank or notary receiving the capital escrow deposit (certificat de dépôt des fonds).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All shareholders sign the statuts; each cash contribution is transferred by wire to a blocked account opened in the company's formation name; the bank or notary issues the deposit certificate identifying the amounts and the escrow release clause that will be lifted only upon RCS registration; if in-kind contributions are made, they must be fully delivered and valued by a commissaire aux apports before the statutory formalities are completed.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts signed by all shareholders
Bank certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Valuation report of any in-kind contributions (rapport des commissaires aux apports)
Shareholders' identity documents and passports
Certificate of residence for the proposed Président (justificatif de domicile)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or notary rejects the escrow opening (e.g. source-of-funds questions), rectify by providing enhanced KYC documents or select an alternative French bank; if statutory defects are found, hold a new shareholders' assembly to amend the statuts before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation Notice in an Approved Legal Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) approved by the prefect for the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the legal notice (avis de constitution) containing the proposed corporate name, form (SAS), capital amount, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and the identity of the Président; deposit the announcement with the approved gazette; retain the recipient's certificate of publication (attestation de parution) which must be included in the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Draft text of the avis de constitution
Project of the statuts for verification of mandatory insertions
Payment of gazette insertion fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette requests corrected wording (e.g. number of shares or Président identity), correct and republish; the attestation de parution remains valid for filing for six months; if delayed beyond this period, a new notice must be published.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Dossier with the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); the platform relays the file to the competent Greffe.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the business account on the INPI portal, select the corporate constitution (formation d'une SAS) form, upload the signed statuts, certificate of capital deposit, publication attestation, declaration of beneficial owner, declaration of the director function, and power of attorney if submitted by an authorised agent; complete the M0 form with the ISIC/NAF code (6499Z if the ACPR authorisation permits it, otherwise a provisional NAF code) and the required legal data; pay the invoice generated by the portal to cover the INPI and greffe tariffs.
required_dossiers: Completed formulaire M0 / administrative data sheet
Signed statuts (PDF copy)
Certificat de dépôt des fonds
Attestation de parution (legal announcement)
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (formulaire BE)
Identity documents and pouvoir/power of attorney of the filer
Compliance letter for the regulated activity where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Guichet unique will return a 'dossier incomplet' notice with a cure period (typically 15 days); complete the missing items and resubmit; after a formal refusal, a new application must be deposited; recourse against rejection lies before the judge charged with supervision of the commercial registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Issuance of the Kbis Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (commercial court registry) of the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the complete dossier, the Greffe examines legal compliance (corporate name, capital, legal form, corporate purpose, identity and criminal records of legal representatives), records the company in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés and delivers the registration number (SIREN) and the official extract Kbis, which constitutes the legal date of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Complete electronic dossier transmitted via the Guichet unique
Proof of criminal record clearance for the Président where requested
Receipt of payment of greffe fees
Copy of the lease or real-estate right for the registered office (justificatif de jouissance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a 'défaut de conformité' or refuses registration, comply with the registry's rectification instructions within the set deadline or file an appeal with the president of the commercial court (procédure d'injonction); if the registered office proof is inadequate, substitute a valid lease or an attestation from the property owner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Administrative Formalisation (Corporate Bank Account, URSSAF and Governance Set-up)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French banking institutions, URSSAF (social security registration), and the company's officers acting under the statuts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Kbis, unlock the blocked capital deposits, open an unrestricted corporate bank account, register the Président under the mandatory social regime (assimilé-salarié status for SAS president or TNS depending on the statuts), register the company with URSSAF, obtain the SIRET number, and implement the statutory corporate file (register of shares, minutes book, shareholders' decisions).
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Original bank certificate of deposit or escrow release confirmation
Président's identity document and proof of address
Statuts and SIREN registration number
Declaration of beneficial owners already filed with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses an account despite the Kbis (anti-money-laundering risk), request the Bank of France's 'droit au compte' procedure under Article L.312-1 of the Code monétaire et financier; if URSSAF registration is delayed, operations may continue, but contributions must be paid once the provisional registration is effective.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via official portal https://www.impots.gouv.fr/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French entities obtain SIREN/SIRET via INSEE and VAT identification number (FR + 11-digit SIREN) through guichet unique or tax authorities; foreign entities register via impots.gouv.fr after establishing French presence or specific procedures
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; French companies may opt into certain regimes such as micro-entreprise for small entities, but SAS defaults to standard corporate taxation with territorial scope

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing (facturation électronique) for all VAT-registered businesses since 2024; API integration with tax authorities for digital stamping and clearance in B2B transactions

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate for exports of goods and cross-border services performed outside France, requiring proof that the transaction is completed abroad
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU), Transport document (Bill of Lading or CMR), Proof of delivery or service performance, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims result in penalties of up to 80% of the evaded VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback of zero-rated VAT and potential criminal sanctions

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) is the central bank; foreign-exchange policy is administered by the Direction générale du Trésor (DG Trésor), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique. Prudential licensing and AML/CFT supervision for banks, payment institutions, electronic money institutions, and crowdfunding service providers are exercised by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR) and the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a euro-area member. The euro (EUR) is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. Exchange controls were abolished; inbound and outbound capital, equity injections, intercompany loans, dividends, royalties, loan repayments, and profit remittances are not subject to prior authorisation or quantitative limits. Profit remittance faces no FX-specific hurdle after corporate tax and withholding tax compliance. Residual frictions arise from AML/CFT, sanctions screening, balance-of-payments statistical reporting, and sector licensing. Banks must verify the purpose and origin of funds, and high-risk fintech activity may trigger enhanced due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts. Resident entities may retain export proceeds in EUR or foreign currency and are not required to convert them within a prescribed timeline. Reporting obligations to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics remain for certain international transactions, generally through the declarative portal and depending on applicable thresholds; these are statistical filings, not FX surrender requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate to high for EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment service providers (PSPs) passporting under PSD2/EMD2; low for non-EU offshore EMIs. EU-licensed EMIs may provide multi-currency accounts, cross-border collections, and wallet payouts, provided client funds are safeguarded in segregated accounts at an EU credit institution or invested in secure low-risk assets. Non-EU EMIs cannot passport into France and must rely on reverse solicitation, local partnership, or a French/EU licence. ACPR authorisation is mandatory for payment services, e-money issuance, and certain lending/crowdfunding models; AMF authorisation is required for crowdfunding service providers under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 and for certain intermediation activities. AML/CFT, sanctions, and consumer-credit rules constrain cross-border viability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not universally mandatory, but French banks and ACPR-supervised institutions commonly require at least one director, beneficial owner, or authorised representative to attend an in-person or live video KYC interview. Remote onboarding is permitted under ACPR guidance where robust identity verification, liveness detection, certified corporate documents, proof of address, and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth evidence are provided. High-risk fintech accounts may require branch attendance, notarised documents, or local substance evidence. Original certified documents, K-bis, UBO register extract, and certified translations are typically mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk ISIC 6499 micro-lending/P2P platform requiring ACPR or AMF licence for consumer credit, payment services, crowdfunding, or intermediation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ACPR/AMF licence or registration; crowdfunding service provider authorisation under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503; IOBSP/IFP registration where applicable; AML/CFT program, MLRO appointment, business-wide risk assessment, and compliance manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex, opaque, or foreign ownership structure with nominee shareholders or layered UBO chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO register extract; K-bis; certificate of incorporation; shareholder register; nominee/trust disclosures; certified translations; ownership chart certified by legal counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds or source of wealth ambiguity for inbound capital injections or shareholder loans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements; bank statements; capital injection purpose memo; loan agreements; investor subscription agreements; tax residency certificates; proof of lawful origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse media hits against directors, UBOs, or platform partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening reports; PEP declarations; sanctions clearance certificates; adverse-media remediation evidence; independent third-party due diligence reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value SEPA direct debits and local wallet payouts indicative of consumer-lending or fraud risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction monitoring policy; fraud and chargeback controls; borrower KYC/CDD procedures; merchant and wallet-partner due diligence; outsourcing agreements and ACPR outsourcing notifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient French physical presence or substance for a licensed financial activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Local directors; registered office lease; payroll and social-security registrations; substance memorandum; French tax registration; governance minutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AML/CFT control weaknesses or prior regulatory findings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ACPR inspection readiness pack; independent AML audit; training records; remediation plan; suspicious transaction reporting procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto-asset, cash-intensive, or high-risk jurisdiction exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: MiCA/CASP registration where applicable; wallet screening policy; counterparty jurisdiction risk assessment; enhanced due diligence files; travel-rule compliance evidence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection is typically executed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV from a shareholder or investor account to the French SAS corporate account. Standard purpose codes include INVESTMENT CAPITAL, EQUITY CAPITAL, SHARE CAPITAL, INTERCOMPANY LOAN, and LOAN. Banks verify the capital-increase documentation, notarised or certified articles, K-bis, shareholder resolutions, UBO data, and source of funds. No prior FX authorisation is required. EUR settlements use TARGET2/T2 or SEPA Credit Transfer; non-EUR injections involve correspondent banking and FX conversion. Balance-of-payments statistical declarations to Banque de France may apply above thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and platform disbursements use SWIFT MT103 for clean payments, MT202 for bank-to-bank transfers, SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for EUR payments, SEPA Core/B2B Direct Debit for collections, and commercial letters of credit or documentary collections under UCP 600 and URR 725. Cross-border trade settlement may use MT700/MT760 for LC issuance and amendment. Micro-lending payouts to borrowers are routed through licensed PSPs/EMIs, local wallet payout partners, or SEPA rails, with reconciliation, sanctions screening, and payment-purpose coding. TARGET2 and SWIFT gpi provide settlement finality and tracking.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-convertible currency exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Société par Actions Simplifiée
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential shareholder or judicial action; directors may incur liability for failure to convene or approve accounts. No automatic administrative strike-off applies solely for late approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts and applicable management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du Tribunal de commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and civil fine generally up to EUR 1,500, potentially EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance. No automatic annual administrative strike-off timetable exists solely for late accounts filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and required schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a 31 December year-end, subject to electronic filing deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty generally 10% of tax due, plus late-payment interest generally 0.20% per month; higher penalties may apply for deliberate or fraudulent conduct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry and French Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation filing; file an update generally within 30 days after a change in beneficial ownership or control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal and financial sanctions may apply to the legal representative for failure to file or inaccurate information; court injunction and potential management restrictions are possible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and prudential or regulatory reporting applicable to the lending platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Applicable supervisory authority, including the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, Autorité des marchés financiers, or other designated authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Reporting dates depend on the entity's authorization, licensing category, and applicable prudential regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Regulatory warnings, corrective measures, administrative fines, license restrictions, suspension, or withdrawal may apply. Exact sanctions depend on the authorization regime.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of three thresholds: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 average employees. Appointment may also be required for qualifying groups, regulated activities, or sector-specific licensing rules. A regulated lending or payment activity may impose additional audit and reporting requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority rules (Autorité des normes comptables). IFRS may apply or be permitted in specific consolidated-accounting circumstances, but statutory standalone SAS accounts generally use French GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual beneficial ownership confirmation. The company must maintain accurate ownership and control information and file an update with the Register of Beneficial Owners after each relevant change, generally within 30 days. Share transfers must be recorded in the shareholders' accounts and share-transfer register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or shareholders' accounts
Register of Directors and corporate officers
Shareholders' decision and meeting minutes book
Beneficial ownership records and supporting documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-1,950 per year for a commercial registered office and corporate secretarial address services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 10,000-30,000 per year for a regulated fintech or lending-platform SAS; smaller non-regulated entities may range from USD 5,000-15,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs (turnover below EUR 10M, held at least 75% by individuals); Research Tax Credit (CIR) of 30%; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) of 20%; Young Innovative Company (JEI) exemption from employer social contributions; 5% social contribution surcharge on corporate income tax for companies with turnover above EUR 7.63M.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD and attached liasse fiscale (Annexes 2052-SD through 2060-SD), filed electronically via EDI/EFI portal on impots.gouv.fr (professionals).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December: 3 May of the following year (shifted to 4 May if 3 May is a Saturday or Sunday). For any other fiscal year: within three months after the close of the fiscal year, extended to the next business day if the three-month anniversary falls on a weekend or public holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN, APE/NAF code, registered office, legal form (SAS), share capital, date of balance sheet close, and authorised representative (President or Director General).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must provide full foreign residential/registered address and attach evidence of a French fiscal representative or fixed establishment if treaty-relevant income is reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-adjusted net profit (bénéfice imposable) for the French entity before loss carry-forwards or intra-group adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents without a French permanent establishment report only French-source income; treaty apportionment schedules are to be added to the return if revenue is allocated via a branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year deficits set off against current-year taxed profits, distinctly from the differences arising on transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only French PE losses; foreign-parent losses are inadmissible; if the company ceased activities, loss utilisation requires a specific declaration under Article 209 CGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detail of intercompany loans, royalties, management charges, and interest paid to non-French related undertakings; used for TP screening and withholding-tax review.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the beneficial owner, attach a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), and state the arm's-length justification; non-resident lenders claiming treaty benefits must also submit a borrower certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic 5% increase of the net tax due; 10% if the return is filed within 30 days after notification; 40% if arising from wilful concealment or fraudulent filing; 80% for simulated or abusive arrangements. Late-payment interest charged at 0.20% per month or 2.40% per year from the due date; criminal fine of up to EUR 500,000 under Article 1741 CGI for counterfeit returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on distributions to non-resident corporate shareholders not covered by the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; 12.8% plus social levies for non-resident individuals (PFU), subject to DTA reductions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the beneficial owner must supply the French paying company with a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) or Form 5000/5001 and evidence of substantive holding (10% minimum and a 24-month holding period for Directive relief; treaty-specific ownership thresholds). The paying company applies the reduced treaty rate at source or files Form 2777-SD to recover any excess withholding; documentation must accompany the quarterly withholding return. Retrospective relief is claimable through the French tax authority within the statutory limitation period, ordinarily by filing a form 2777-SD accompanied by the TRC of the foreign recipient.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding under Articles 182 B and 219 sexies CGI at 33.33% on a taxable base of 70% of gross royalties, yielding effective 23.33%; treaty rates usually reduced to 0%–10% (e.g., 10% on patent remittances) with DTA certificate. Interest: no general withholding tax on interest paid to non-resident corporate lenders; treaty-protected at 0% in most cases; interest paid to a non-resident individual is subject to the 12.8% flat tax, while non-cooperative jurisdiction payments are denied deduction and subject to a 75% withholding-equivalent tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million group consolidated turnover or total assets; additional mandatory declaration for intercompany payments to non-residents exceeding EUR 100,000 per annum via Form 2257-SD. Local File and Master File must be maintained at the French fiscal seat within 30 days of a request by the tax administration.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies no Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) of the offshore type, but imposes an effective place-of-management doctrine, Article 165 bis CGI and anti-abuse rules (Article L.64 LPF, EU ATAD). The SAS must demonstrate actual decisions, staff, premises, and real lending operations in France, otherwise tax benefits, treaty access, and Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief are denied as artificial arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Fraudulent Omission in CIT Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally failing to declare interest or platform fee income from the peer-to-peer lending ledger; overstating bad-debt reserves or charging fictitious expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative: 40% fraud penalty, 80% penalty for abusive arrangement, plus late-payment interest (0.20% per month). Criminal: under Article 1741 CGI, up to EUR 500,000 fine and five years' imprisonment; the fine may be doubled to the amount of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers are jointly and severally liable for the tax, penalties, and interest under Article L.267 LPF; may face imprisonment, placement on a French travel ban (interdiction de quitter le territoire), prohibition on managing a business, and civil restitution of unpaid corporate taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a nominee shell, with no real employees, premises, or lending activity, to derive treaty withholding relief or to divert profits to low-tax jurisdiction shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article L.64 LPF abuse of law doctrine: restatement of the entire arrangement, additional income tax, 80% aggravation penalty, and denial of DTA benefits; if part of a sham, the tax administration can disregard the legal entity and tax the recipient/parent directly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president of the SAS may be personally assessed for the taxes re-determined; possible civil liability for damages, criminal prosecution under Article 1743 CGI for fraudulent registration or concealment, and international travel bans to guarantee execution of the assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a peer-to-peer micro-lending platform or collecting lender funds without ACPR authorisation or ORIAS consumer-credit registration (IO2/IF), and failure to comply with TRACFIN filing duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions under Articles L.571-4 and L.541-8 of the French Monetary and Financial Code: up to EUR 750,000 fine and five years' imprisonment for illegal exercise of credit operations; ACPR administrative penalties up to EUR 100 million or 10% of annual turnover; licence withdrawal and injunction to cease business; interest on unlawful loans is void.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers face criminal conviction, automatic prohibition on corporate management, travel bans, and personal orders for restitution of interest or commissions; assets can be seized as security in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or file the Master File/Local File/Form 2257-SD when group thresholds are exceeded; entering into intra-group interest, service, or royalty contracts that deviate from the arm's-length principle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed fine of EUR 15,000 for non-disclosure of Form 2257-SD (Article 1732 ter CGI); transfer-pricing adjustment is supplemented by a 40% penalty for clearly fictitious acts and 0.20% monthly interest; in case of abuse, 80% penalty (Article 1729 CGI). Criminal exposure can arise if deliberate concealment exceeds 10%, plus a potential fine of EUR 500,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative who knowingly executes or approves non-arm's-length pricing is jointly liable for the resulting tax and penalties; personal civil damages may be claimed by minority shareholders and the fiscal administration; the court may order an anti-departure order and confiscation of corporate assets.
